PEACHTREE PANTRY & BEVERAGE CO. (PPB) 
EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK 
Document ID: PPB-HB-2026-V1 
Version: 1.0 
Effective Date: February 1, 2026 
Status: Active 
 
1. WELCOME TO PEACHTREE 
Congratulations on joining Peachtree Pantry & Beverage Co. (PPB)! You are now part of a 
team of over 250 professionals across Georgia, New York, and Virginia. This handbook is 
designed for our most valuable assets—our front-line service employees, including our 
Front-line Service Associates, Shift Leads, and Hotline Cooks. 
2. OUR CORE VALUES 
• 
Integrity: We act with honesty and never compromise the truth. 
• 
Community: We serve our local neighborhoods in Atlanta, Richmond, and NYC with 
pride. 
• 
Safety: We maintain the highest standards of food safety and sanitation. 
3. DIVERSITY & EQUAL OPPORTUNITY (EEO) 
PPB provides equal employment opportunities to all employees without regard to race, 
creed, color, religion, gender, or national origin. We comply with all applicable state and 
local laws in Georg

• 
Accommodations: We reasonably accommodate qualified individuals with 
disabilities in accordance with the ADA. 
4. EMPLOYEE CLASSIFICATIONS 
To ensure accurate payroll and benefit administration, PPB utilizes the following categories: 
• 
Full-time Regular: Scheduled for 30+ hours per week. 
• 
Part-time Regular: Scheduled for fewer than 30 hours per week. 
• 
Front-line Roles: This includes Hotline Cooks, Front-line Service Associates, and 
Shift Leads. 
• 
Exempt vs. Non-Exempt: Most front-line roles are non-exempt and eligible for 
overtime. 
5. COMPENSATION & TIMEKEEPING 
• 
Payday: PPB operates on a biweekly payroll schedule. 
•

ION & TIMEKEEPING 
• 
Payday: PPB operates on a biweekly payroll schedule. 
• 
Time Records: All non-exempt employees must clock in/out via the Point of Sale 
(POS) system. No work may be performed "off the clock". 
+1 
• 
Tipped Employees: If an employee's tips + hourly wage do not meet the state 
minimum wage (GA, NY, or VA), PPB will pay the difference. 
• 
Meal Breaks: Employees working 7.5+ continuous hours are entitled to a 30-minute 
unpaid meal period. 
6. REGIONAL SICK LEAVE OVERRIDES 
• 
Georgia Locations: Employees accrue 1 hour of sick leave for every 40 hours 
worked, up to 40 hours per year. 
• 
New York Locations: In accordance with NY State law, employees at PPB (as a mid-
sized employer) receive up to 40 hours of paid sick leave per year. 
• 
Virginia Locations: Employees follow the standard PPB accrual rate of 1 hour per 
40 worked.

7. WORKPLACE EXPECTATIONS & SAFETY 
• 
Appearance: Hair must be neatly trimmed and tied back if shoulder-length. Visible 
tattoos are permitted unless they contain offensive imagery. 
+1 
• 
The Hotline Cook Standard: Hotline Cooks must wear non-slip, closed-toe shoes 
at all times to prevent injury from spills or dropped equipment. Open-back clogs are 
prohibited. 
+1 
• 
Personal Cell Phones: Use is forbidden while on duty except in extreme 
emergencies. 
+1 
• 
Sanitation: All food-handling employees must wash hands after using the restroom, 
sneezing, or touching raw food. 
+1 
8. LEAVES OF ABSENCE 
• 
FMLA: Employees who have worked for PPB for 12 months and 1,250 hours are 
eligible for up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave for serious health conditions or the 
birth/adoption of a child. 
+2 
• 
Bereavement: Regular employees are eligible for up to 3 days of paid leave 
following the death of an immediate family member.

9. GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE 
If you have a concern regarding your working conditions: 
1. Discuss it with your Shift Lead. 
2. If unresolved, escalate to the General Manager. 
3. If still unresolved, contact your regional HR Representative.
